---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/isso-comments/isso
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: ghcr.io/isso-comments/isso:0.14.0
  port: 8080
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: none (Isso is SQLite-only; the volume IS the database)
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0174
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: isso
quirks:
  - "⛔ ASK FOR THE WEBSITE FIRST. THIS DEPLOY CANNOT BE PLANNED WITHOUT IT. Isso is a comment server for somebody else's site: it renders nothing of its own, and its URL is an API endpoint that the site embeds. isso/__init__.py:187-189: when [general] host is empty, make_app logs \"No website(s) configured, Isso won't work.\" and calls sys.exit(1). Because the image's ENTRYPOINT runs gunicorn with --preload, that exit happens in the master process, so the container dies at boot, redu's hostname answers 502 forever, and the only clue is one ERROR line in the log. Get the site's full origin (scheme and host, for example https://example.com) from the user BEFORE you plan anything. If the site is not live yet that is fine: isso/__init__.py:191-202 HEADs each host at boot with a 5 second timeout and only WARNS when it cannot reach it."
  - "⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: THIS APP HAS NO ACCOUNTS AT ALL. Nobody signs up and nobody is an owner. Commenters are anonymous by design; the only privileged thing is the moderation UI at /admin/, which is gated by ONE shared password read straight out of the config file, compared as a plain string ([REDACTED:value]:1444-1445). Two facts make this safe or unsafe at deploy time and nothing decides it later. FIRST, [admin] enabled defaults to FALSE (isso/isso.cfg:68-69), and while it is off both /admin/ and /login/ render a fixed \"disabled\" page, so there is no administrator to become. SECOND, the password shipped in isso/isso.cfg:72 is a literal that anyone can read in the repository, so enabling admin without replacing it hands the moderation queue to the internet. This recipe enables admin and supplies a generated password from the container environment at deploy time, so the window never opens. There is no first-visitor race to lose, and there is nothing to claim afterwards."
  - "⛔⛔ AN UNSET ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE BECOMES THE PASSWORD, SILENTLY. This is the sharpest trap in the file and it is a property of Python rather than of Isso. isso/config.py:105-107 runs os.path.expandvars over every config value, which is what lets the config say password = [REDACTED:value] and take the real value from the container env. But expandvars leaves an UNDEFINED variable as its literal text, so if the variable is missing from the compose environment the admin password silently becomes that literal placeholder string, exactly as it is written in this very file, which is to say a password everyone who read this recipe already knows. Nothing errors and the login page looks normal. The verification script in the body proves BOTH halves: that the literal placeholder is refused, and that your real value is accepted. Never skip the first half; on its own the second proves only that you can log in."
  - "⛔ SET dbpath OR EVERY COMMENT LIVES IN /tmp. isso/isso.cfg:8 defaults dbpath to /tmp/comments.db, and its own comment says to change it. The image declares VOLUME /db (Dockerfile:91-94) and nothing connects the two, so a deploy that copies the default config comes up perfectly healthy and loses every comment on the next container restart. Set dbpath = /db/comments.db and mount a NAMED volume there. PROVE IT AFTER BOOT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a negative check alone is worthless: the docker block in the body of this file asserts that comments.db EXISTS under /db, which is what tells you the exec command worked at all, before it asserts that nothing is under /tmp."
  - "⛔ THE SESSION KEY LIVES IN THE DATABASE, WHICH MAKES THE VOLUME THE ONLY THING PROTECTING IT. isso/__init__.py:100-101 builds the signer from db.preferences.get(\"session-key\"), and isso/config.py:169-170 says outright that the old [general] session-key option is now stored in the database itself. So there is no secret to set and nothing to remember: lose the volume and you lose the comments AND the key that signs the admin-session cookie and every author edit, delete and moderation link. Outstanding e-mail moderation links stop working. Nothing errors. Back up the SQLite file; redu's managed-database backups do not apply here, because there is no managed database."
  - "⛔ THERE IS NO DATABASE OPTION. DO NOT PROVISION A MANAGED POSTGRES FOR THIS. isso/__init__.py:100 constructs db.SQLite3 unconditionally and SQLite is the only backend in the source. A managed database would bill at GBP 0.0174/hr and hold nothing. The volume is the database."
  - "⛔ MOUNT A CONFIG FILE, AND KNOW WHAT HAPPENS IF YOU DO NOT. The image sets ENV ISSO_SETTINGS=/config/isso.cfg (Dockerfile:96) and isso/run.py:16 passes it straight to config.load, which opens it with NO existence check. Miss the mount and gunicorn's workers die on a FileNotFoundError traceback in a boot loop, which reads like a broken image rather than a missing file. (The isso CLI checks and prints a clean error, isso/__init__.py:263-267, but the container does not use that path.) Ship the config as a read-only bind mount from the uploaded source directory: Isso never writes it, and keeping it in the source means the next redeploy carries the same settings. The SECRET does not go in it; the file references $ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD and the value arrives from the compose environment."
  - "SET public-endpoint TO THE FULL https URL, WHICH MEANS GENERATING THE HOSTNAME YOURSELF FIRST. It is not cosmetic. [REDACTED:value]:434-449 decides the Secure flag and the SameSite value of every cookie by whether public-endpoint (or the auto-detected host) starts with https://: https gives Secure with SameSite=None, which is what a comment box on YOUR domain talking to a redu hostname needs, and anything else gives SameSite=Lax, which quietly breaks the author's own edit and delete window from a third-party page. So generate the dname up front, in full <app>-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form, and set public-endpoint to https://<that> with NO trailing slash: isso/config.py:183-192 warns about a trailing slash today and says a future version may refuse to start."
  - "TURN MODERATION ON, AND UNDERSTAND WHY THIS ONE IS NOT PARANOIA. moderation defaults to FALSE (isso/isso.cfg:74-78), which publishes every comment the instant it is posted. The endpoint is public by necessity and [REDACTED:value]:363-371 shows that a caller who supplies a title can create an ARBITRARY thread rather than one that exists on your site, so the spam surface is not limited to your real pages. [guard] is on by default at 2 comments per minute per /24 (isso/isso.cfg:170-178), which slows a bot down rather than stopping one. Set moderation enabled = true, and note the consequence: with notify = stdout and no SMTP configured, the ONLY way to approve anything is the admin UI, so moderation and admin have to be turned on together or the queue never drains."
  - "SET YOUR OWN [hash] salt AT DEPLOY TIME, BEFORE ANYONE COMMENTS. isso/isso.cfg:249-252 ships a fixed salt and says plainly it has been the same since release and is identical across installations, so identicons match everywhere. Its stated job is protecting commenters' e-mail addresses from rainbow tables, and a published shared salt does not do that. Generate your own alphanumeric value. Do it BEFORE the first comment: changing it later changes every existing identicon, because the hash is what draws them."
  - "PORT 8080, AND DO NOT CHASE [server] listen. Dockerfile:95,99 expose 8080 and the ENTRYPOINT binds gunicorn to 0.0.0.0:8080 with 4 workers. The listen = http://localhost:8080 line in the default config only affects the standalone isso run server (isso/__init__.py:295-302) and is INERT under the image, so do not \"fix\" it and do not assume it made the app listen anywhere. Pass 8080 to deploy_compose. Gate every check on GET /info, which is public and returns JSON with a version key (isso/views/__init__.py:47-88, and it is what upstream's own compose health check uses): redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts, and an error page passes every assertion phrased as \"did it NOT do X\"."
  - "PIN FROM ghcr.io, NOT DOCKER HUB, AND NOT :latest. The official image is ghcr.io/isso-comments/isso; docker.io/isso/isso does not exist and the Docker Hub API returns object not found for it, so every isso image on Docker Hub is somebody's fork. ⚠️ Measured on 2026-08-17 with an identical Accept header on every call: the tags 0.14.0, 0.14 and release all resolve to sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:c59db3f5», while latest resolves to a DIFFERENT digest, sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:4fa5aeaa». On this repository latest is NOT the newest release, and there is also a dev tag. Use ghcr.io/isso-comments/isso:0.14.0."
  - "trusted-proxies AFFECTS VOTE FAIRNESS AND IS UNVERIFIED ON redu. [REDACTED:value]:420-432 walks X-Forwarded-For backwards and takes the first address NOT listed in [server] trusted-proxies, then anonymises it. That address is what the per-subnet vote and rate limiting keys on, so with the option unset every visitor may look like the same proxy and share one budget. Nobody has run this on redu yet, so DO NOT guess a value into the config: deploy, look at what the container actually reports as the client address, and only then set trusted-proxies and write the finding back into this file."
  - "NOTIFICATIONS ARE stdout UNLESS YOU CONFIGURE SMTP, AND reply-notifications IS A SPAM LEVER. notify defaults to stdout (isso/isso.cfg:44), meaning new comments are logged and nothing is e-mailed. Configuring [smtp] gets you moderation links by e-mail, and the config file wants the SMTP password in plain text, so use the same $VARIABLE trick rather than writing it into the file. reply-notifications defaults to false and upstream's own comment (isso/isso.cfg:46-49) says turning it on without moderation makes Isso an easy way to send spam. Leave it off unless the user asks and moderation is on."
  - "A MISSPELLED OPTION IS A WARNING, NOT AN ERROR. isso/config.py:148-171 loads the shipped defaults first and then your file, and anything in yours that was not in theirs is logged as \"no such option: [section] key\" and otherwise ignored. So a typo in a setting you were relying on for safety, moderation or admin included, leaves the DEFAULT in force while the container starts perfectly. Read the first twenty lines of the container log after every deploy and treat any \"no such option\" line as a failure to fix."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER. Checked the README, the Dockerfile, the default config and the compose: there is no RAM figure anywhere. m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB, 20 GB disk) is reasoning from \"a small Python WSGI app on alpine, four gunicorn workers, SQLite, serving a handful of JSON endpoints and one minified script\", not a measurement. Comment text is tiny, so neither memory nor disk is likely to be the constraint. Record the real idle figure on the first run: it is the single most useful thing that run can add."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> ask the user for the website origin(s) Isso will serve, since the container EXITS without at least one -> generate the dname yourself and use it for public-endpoint -> generate a long alphanumeric admin password and a fresh salt -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.017/hr, roughly GBP 13 a month, and it fits inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), NO database, port 8080, a named volume on /db and the config bind-mounted read-only at /config/isso.cfg. ⚠️ plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large once needs_compose is declared: pass flavor_id explicitly to hold m1.small, since that larger floor exists for things that BUILD from source and this image is pulled."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source. ## The three that actually break it

**No website, no container.** With `[general] host` empty, Isso calls `sys.exit(1)` at startup
rather than serving. Because the entrypoint preloads, the container dies and the hostname answers
502 forever, with one ERROR line in the log as the only clue.

**The database defaults to `/tmp`.** The image declares a volume at `/db` and the shipped
config points at `/tmp/comments.db`. Nothing connects them for you. It comes up healthy and loses
every comment on the next restart.

**An unset variable becomes the password.** Python's `expandvars` leaves an undefined variable
as its literal text, so a missing `ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD` makes the admin password the placeholder
string printed in this file. The script below proves the placeholder is refused before it proves
your real one is accepted.

## Prove the admin password took

# Prove this Isso's moderation UI is behind YOUR password and not the placeholder.
#   ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] ./verify-admin.sh isso-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = good, 1 = BAD (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -u
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-admin.sh <host>}"
: "${ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD:«REDACTED:assigned:52ed1607» the password you deployed with, so this can prove it works}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# (1) GATE AND POSITIVE CONTROL. /info is public and app-specific. Without it every assertion
#     below is vacuous, because redu's proxy answers 502 while the container starts and an error
#     page refuses logins just as convincingly as a correctly configured Isso does.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/info" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/info") || code=000
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /info answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
    echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the container starts. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
    echo "  If it stays 502, read the log: Isso EXITS at boot when [general] host is empty," >&2
    echo "  and when it has exited there is nothing serving to be checked." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
grep -q '"version"' "$TMP/info" || {
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /info returned 200 but the body is not Isso's." >&2; exit 2; }

cat "$TMP/info"; echo

#     container, expandvars left this exact literal in the config and it IS the password.
#     Bodies go through a file, never argv, so nothing lands in ps.
printf 'password=[REDACTED:value]' '$ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD' > "$TMP/bad"
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary @"$TMP/bad" \
  "https://$HOST/login/") || code=000

  echo "the admin password is a string published in the recipe. Fix the compose environment and" >&2
  echo "redeploy before anyone finds /admin/." >&2
  exit 1

#     page with 200; a correct one redirects to /admin/ ([REDACTED:value]:1445-1449).

  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary @"$TMP/good" \
  "https://$HOST/login/") || loc=""
case "$loc" in
  */admin/) echo "PASS: [REDACTED:value] password logs in, the placeholder does not." ; exit 0 ;;
  "")

    echo "SOMETHING is refusing logins. Either the password differs from what was deployed, or" >&2
    echo "[admin] enabled is false, in which case /login/ renders a fixed disabled page and there" >&2
    echo "is no moderation UI at all. Check the container log and the mounted config." >&2
    exit 2 ;;

## The three that actually break it

**No website, no container.** With `[general] host` empty, Isso calls `sys.exit(1)` at startup
rather than serving. Because the entrypoint preloads, the container dies and the hostname answers
502 forever, with one ERROR line in the log as the only clue.

**The database defaults to `/tmp`.** The image declares a volume at `/db` and the shipped
config points at `/tmp/comments.db`. Nothing connects them for you. It comes up healthy and loses
every comment on the next restart.

**An unset variable becomes the password.** Python's `expandvars` leaves an undefined variable
as its literal text, so a missing `ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD` makes the admin password the placeholder
string printed in this file. The script below proves the placeholder is refused before it proves
your real one is accepted.

## Prove the admin password took

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this Isso's moderation UI is behind YOUR password and not the placeholder.
#   ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] ./verify-admin.sh isso-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = good, 1 = BAD (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -u
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-admin.sh <host>}"
: "${ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD:«REDACTED:assigned:52ed1607» the password you deployed with, so this can prove it works}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# (1) GATE AND POSITIVE CONTROL. /info is public and app-specific. Without it every assertion
#     below is vacuous, because redu's proxy answers 502 while the container starts and an error
#     page refuses logins just as convincingly as a correctly configured Isso does.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/info" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/info") || code=000
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /info answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
    echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the container starts. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
    echo "  If it stays 502, read the log: Isso EXITS at boot when [general] host is empty," >&2
    echo "  and when it has exited there is nothing serving to be checked." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
grep -q '"version"' "$TMP/info" || {
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /info returned 200 but the body is not Isso's." >&2; exit 2; }
echo "OK: Isso is serving. /info says:"
cat "$TMP/info"; echo

# (2) THE NEGATIVE. The placeholder must NOT log in. If ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD never reached the
#     container, expandvars left this exact literal in the config and it IS the password.
#     Bodies go through a file, never argv, so nothing lands in ps.
printf 'password=[REDACTED:value]' '$ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD' > "$TMP/bad"
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary @"$TMP/bad" \
  "https://$HOST/login/") || code=000
if [ "$code" = "302" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: the literal placeholder LOGGED IN. The variable never reached the container, so" >&2
  echo "the admin password is a string published in the recipe. Fix the compose environment and" >&2
  echo "redeploy before anyone finds /admin/." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# (3) THE POSITIVE, which is what makes step 2 mean anything. A wrong password renders the login
#     page with 200; a correct one redirects to /admin/ ([REDACTED:value]:1445-1449).
printf 'password=[REDACTED:value]' "$ISSO_ADMIN_PASSWORD" > "$TMP/good"
loc=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-binary @"$TMP/good" \
  "https://$HOST/login/") || loc=""
case "$loc" in
  */admin/) echo "PASS: [REDACTED:value] password logs in, the placeholder does not." ; exit 0 ;;
  "")
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: your password did not redirect either, so this script proved only that" >&2
    echo "SOMETHING is refusing logins. Either the password differs from what was deployed, or" >&2
    echo "[admin] enabled is false, in which case /login/ renders a fixed disabled page and there" >&2
    echo "is no moderation UI at all. Check the container log and the mounted config." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  *)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: login redirected to '$loc', which is not /admin/." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
esac
```

## Prove the database is on the volume

Both halves, on the VM. The `/db` check is what proves your commands run at all; without it the
empty `/tmp` result would be worthless.

```bash
C=isso   # confirm with: sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}}'

# Positive: must print the pinned image. If this errors, everything below is void.
sudo docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' "$C"

# The assertion: /db is a real mount, not a directory inside the container.
sudo docker inspect -f '{{json .Mounts}}' "$C" | grep -c '"Destination":"/db"'   # must be 1

# Positive: the database is really there, which is what makes the next line meaningful.
sudo docker exec "$C" ls /db  | grep -c 'comments.db'                            # must be 1

# The negative: nothing fell back to the shipped default path.
sudo docker exec "$C" ls /tmp | grep -c 'comments.db'                            # must be 0

# And read the first lines of the log: a mistyped option is a warning, not an error.
sudo docker logs "$C" 2>&1 | head -20 | grep -c 'no such option'                 # must be 0
sudo docker logs "$C" 2>&1 | grep -c 'Using database at'                         # must be >= 1
```

## Embedding it

Two lines on the page where you want comments. Replace the hostname with yours.

```html
<script data-isso="https://isso-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud/"
        src="https://isso-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud/js/embed.min.js"></script>
<section id="isso-thread"></section>
```

The site's origin must be listed under `[general] host` in the config, because that list is
also the CORS allowlist. Post a comment from your own page and confirm it appears in
`/admin/`: that round trip, not a health check, is what proves this deploy works.

        src="https://isso-e4ta53ny.redu.cloud/js/embed.min.js"></script>

```

And `trusted-proxies` turned out not to need setting: a comment from [ip] stored `remote_addr` [ip], the real visitor's own /24, so rate limits and votes are already per-visitor.
